t: Wow! I'm alive! Thank you for colouring me so beautifully!
d: Picture: you just opened your eyes, you're wearing brand-new colours, and the child who painted you is right there. 'Wow' is a real jolt; the rest is a warm laugh, like praising a five-year-old.

t: Listen! The trumpet of heaven sounds for you!
d: Picture: you stand high on a cloud speaking to a whole square of people below. Pause half a beat after 'Listen!', then deliver word by word; let the last word ring.

t: Your drawing is lovely, I adore these colours!
m: Gentle praise, kneeling down to a child
d: Picture: you're crouching in front of a child looking at the picture in their hands. Slower; smile on 'lovely'; mean 'adore'.

t: May your day be safe and happy!
d: Picture: the child is about to sleep and you say this at the bedside. Softer, every word clear; a tiny pause before 'and happy'.

t: Draw me a new dress next time!
d: Picture: you're the child's friend begging for one more picture. Lift the end of the sentence; a little giggle is welcome.
Picture: the moment your feet leave the ground. Short, punchy, upwards.
Picture: first time you see your own wings. From low to high, like watching fireworks.
Picture: the child drew you a silly big nose. Breathe in, laugh out, don't hold back. Three takes, each a different laugh.

t: Once upon a time there was a guardian angel who loved children's drawings most of all.
d: Picture: bedtime story voice. Slow, low, a pause after 'Once upon a time', like opening the first page.
